wg-029.text: Is recruited by Den into defense and switches his studies to cryptography.

wg-030.text: Is named national champion when the final is cancelled, and says he does not want to win like this.
flags: Zei is named national champion when the final is cancelled | The blocks say Zei is called “the champion this year” after the finals are cancelled, but they do not specify that he is the “national” champion.

wg-031.text: Supervises the drone battle for Northshore.
flags: Zei supervises the drone battle for Northshore. | The cited block says Zei supervises all fronts and identifies changes in drone combat, but does not specify that the supervision is for Northshore.

wg-032.text: Close friend of Fin; rival, then ally and friend, of Bai; friend of Deluin.
flags: Close friend of Fin | blocks only show Fin and Zei getting off the autobus together, no indication they are close friends.
rival, then ally and friend, of Bai | blocks show Bai beating Zei three times (rivalry) but give no evidence that Zei later becomes an ally or friend.
friend of Deluin | block contains a compliment to Deluin but does not state that Zei is a friend of Deluin.

wg-034.text: Zei's friend in Pafogai Du, a student training with the Bansunpei.
flags: Zei's friend in Pafogai Du | The cited blocks show Fin and Zei together and Fin mentions training with the Bansunpei, but they never state that Fin is Zei's friend nor that he is in Pafogai Du.

wg-035.text: Explains that Dzegoban is coordination training, and that the Bansunpei used its channels to change Dzego's habits after Redshire.

wg-036.text: Helps build the attack on the Arctic drones' AI with Bansunpei researchers.
flags: Fin: Helps build the attack on the Arctic drones' AI with Bansunpei researchers. | The cited blocks only show Fin responded quickly and discuss Bansunpei people’s expertise, but they never state that Fin helped build the attack with Bansunpei researchers.

wg-037.text: Bai Jahen, Zei's Minpentai rival in Pafogai Du.
flags: Bai Jahen, Zei's Minpentai rival in Pafogai Du. | Blocks show Bai Jahen is listed on team Zau alongside Zei Leimin (c4-b90) and that Bai has beaten Zei three times (c4-b72), but they are not described as Minpentai rivals, nor is any Minpentai rivalry between them mentioned.

wg-038.text: Losing what she has: her parents died in a lab explosion, and all she had was her success.

wg-039.text: Success as proof she is strong; she later says Zei's curiosity was a purer motive.

wg-040.text: Learns to cooperate with Zei, then gives him advice and hugs as a friend.

wg-041.text: Considers spending a year in Thaldur to understand the Arctics.

wg-042.text: An older woman in Dzego who knows Zei, at the Minpentai games.
flags: An older woman in Dzego who knows Zei, at the Minpentai games. | The cited blocks mention an older woman noticing someone (c4-b62) and a greeting to Zei (c4-b63) but do not state that the older woman knows Zei, nor do they mention the Minpentai games or place the scene at that event.

wg-043.text: Explains that Minpentai is military training; later works with the Kungaupei.
flags: Mu explains that Minpentai is military training | The blocks contain the statement “It’s military training.” but do not attribute that explanation to Mu.
later works with the Kungaupei | No cited block mentions Mu working with the Kungaupei.

wg-044.text: Saves the rescue of Tafindel with a new plan, and takes over Group South when Den is lost.
flags: Saves the rescue of Tafindel with a new plan | The cited blocks mention Mu proposing a new plan, but they contain no reference to rescuing Tafindel.

wg-045.text: A High Council member of the Kungaupei.

wg-046.text: To recruit Zei into defense; after Redshire, for the shadow society to become the society.
flags: after Redshire | the cited blocks do not indicate that Den’s recruitment of Zei occurs after Redshire.

wg-047.text: Leads Group South in the battle for Northshore and is almost certainly killed when a rear base is hit.

wg-048.text: A contestant from Redshire at Dzego's national championship.
flags: A contestant from Redshire at Dzego's national championship. | The blocks state Deluin is a contestant from Redshire at the national Minpentai championship, not Dzego's.

wg-049.text: Trapped by the invasion; his parents side with the Arctics, and he plays along to win their trust.
flags: Trapped by the invasion | The cited blocks do not state that Deluin is “trapped by the invasion”; they describe his parents’ cooperation with the Arctics and his decision to play along to win their trust, but give no explicit claim that he is trapped.

wg-050.text: Becomes an Arctic commander and helps Veridia break the southern flank.

wg-051.text: Befriends Zei at the nationals and invites him to Redshire.
flags: Deluin befriends Zei at the nationals and invites him to Redshire. | The cited blocks contain no mention of Zei, no reference to the nationals, and only a vague invitation to Redshire without identifying Deluin as the speaker, so the claim is not supported.

wg-052.text: Gladias and Seila's daughter, who struggles at school.

wg-053.text: Is drawn to Arctic propaganda and runs away to Arctic-held Northglade.

wg-054.text: Argues back at her Arctic teacher, is put in detention, and wants to come home.

wg-056.text: Wins a Helisport game; stays in touch with Lily and learns where she is.

wg-057.text: Teenage son of Vil and Daia, the co-family; studies computer science.

wg-058.text: Daughter of Vil and Daia; good at mathematics.

wg-059.text: With Hreda, takes refuge in Northglade's Greater Plum Harbor when Northshore is invaded.

wg-060.text: Uncle Vil, co-parent with Aunt Daia; part of a class action by Jump's former employees against the hedge fund Divergent.
flags: part of a class action by Jump's former employees against the hedge fund Divergent | the cited blocks describe a class action by former Jump employees, but none of them mention Uncle Vil participating in it.

wg-061.text: Seila's friend in Freetown, a researcher at the Freetown Economics Institute.

wg-062.text: Introduces Zei to Freetown's defense companies through the Institute's director.
flags: Jahn introduces Zei to Freetown's defense companies through the Institute's director. | The blocks say Jahn only connected Zei to the Economics Institute director, and the director made the connection to the defense companies.

wg-063.text: A Veridian senator who questioned Gladias at his hearing.
flags: Verdow: A Veridian senator who questioned Gladias at his hearing. | The blocks address Verdow as a senator and invite him to ask a question, but do not state he is Veridian nor that he actually questioned Gladias; they only show a prompt to Gladias to discuss his background.

wg-064.text: Proposes using the courts to replace the failed military leadership.
flags: Verdow proposes using the courts to replace the failed military leadership. | The cited blocks do not contain Verdow’s proposal; they only note the law, that the military failed, and that courts can fire them, but they do not show Verdow explicitly proposing to use the courts to replace the military leadership.

wg-065.text: The Arctic ambassador to Veridia, who argues that only economic growth compounds.

wg-066.text: President of Veridia National University, who debates Ephelion.

wg-067.text: A respected Veridian general who becomes head general and commands the battle for Northshore.
flags: Lektor commands the battle for Northshore | the cited blocks do not mention Northshore or any battle that Lektor commands.

wg-069.text: The son of Redshire's president, held by the Arctics and rescued by the Kungaupei.
flags: rescued by the Kungaupei | The cited blocks say Tafindel is safe in Arturia after being rescued, but they never mention the Kungaupei as the rescuers.

wg-070.text: Zei's mother; Freetown is her first trip abroad.

wg-071.text: A Minpentai priest and an organizer of the nationals.
flags: Su is a Minpentai priest | The cited blocks do not state that Su is a Minpentai priest; they only mention six people in Minpentai priest robes waiting, without identifying Su as one.

wg-072.text: A country of trees and medieval-style stone houses; its capital is Meldan.

wg-073.text: Veridia's capital, with the forest-like Kalimar district, sky bridges and a tree-covered mountain.

wg-074.text: A walled enclave in Meldan, "almost like a country inside a country"; many Veridians push its land taxes up.

wg-075.text: Its buildings are uniform, futuristic glass and steel, unlike the rest of Veridia.

wg-076.text: A country that lost a war to the Arctics a century ago and grows its strength in small, spread-out workshops.

wg-077.text: A Dzego city of small electronics shops and factories on a regular street grid.

wg-078.text: A half-kilometer pyramid at its southern edge is a refurbished mountain holding part of the government.

wg-079.text: Dzego's capital; the name means "main city".

wg-080.text: Cities that elect a share of each other's parliaments, called co-governance.

wg-081.text: A city of the United Cities, mixed rich and run-down, with the Freetown Economics Institute.

wg-082.text: A country of castles, pine forests and red snowy mountains.

wg-083.text: Invaded and annexed by the Arctic Empire.

wg-084.text: A Veridian town in the province of Northshore, near the Arctic border, with Veridia's best math university.

wg-085.text: Taken by the Arctics, except its Greater Plum Harbor, which they leave alone.

wg-086.text: An island of the Arctic core territory east of Northshore, taken by Veridian sea drones.
flags: taken by Veridian sea drones | the blocks say the island was taken by seaborne drones, without specifying them as Veridian sea drones.

wg-087.text: An Arctic city like a giant ice crystal, with a kilometer-tall tower.

wg-088.text: Snowy pine forest in Veridia where the battle for Northshore begins.
flags: Elenar Forest: Snowy pine forest in Veridia where the battle for Northshore begins. | The blocks describe Elenar Forest as a snowy pine forest in Veridia, but they do not say that the battle for Northshore begins there.

wg-089.text: A government-linked, decentralized collective that sets Veridia's taxes and subsidies instead of bans.

wg-090.text: Keepers vote on tax rubrics; Sentinels audit businesses; Acolytes are members in training.

wg-091.text: Anyone can guess a member's task for a bounty, so members keep their roles private.

wg-092.text: Each rubric has twenty-one Keepers in three groups of seven that discuss separately and don't know who is in the other groups; thirteen votes pass a change.

wg-093.text: Order members picked at random to retire and explain the Order to the public, transparent only once they have no power.

wg-094.text: Five judges per case, chosen at random from a large pool and anonymous; an appeal draws a new sample.

wg-095.text: Public funding split down a graph, each node's share decided by a randomly selected committee.

wg-096.text: Public matching of donations; attacked by Bluewhale and later at larger scale by the Arctics.

wg-097.text: Veridia's transparent parliament; a committee of twenty senators approves new Order members.
flags: a committee of twenty senators approves new Order members. | The blocks describe twenty senators seated in a room and mention Parliament committees approving roles such as Keepers, Sentinels, and Court judges, but they do not state that a committee of twenty senators approves new Order members.

wg-098.text: Public meetings, some run by Heralds, whose results Keepers check when debating rubrics.

wg-099.text: Dzego's Decentralized University, which runs by anonymous cryptographic coordination.
flags: Dzego's Decentralized University | The cited blocks refer to DU simply as the "Decentralized University" and describe its anonymous cryptographic coordination, but they do not state that it belongs to or is owned by Dzego.

wg-100.text: The priests who keep improving the Dzegoban language, testing versions across the country.

wg-101.text: Dzego's secret society for defense, a shadow army.

wg-102.text: The Veridian privacy robe: a loose dark purple garment covering the body from hood to ankles.

wg-103.text: A band that picks up silent, whispered speech.

wg-104.text: The local AI on Gladias's hand device.

wg-105.text: Watches and gates verify devices and credentials while learning nothing else.

wg-106.text: A common material lining rooms to block wireless signals.

wg-107.text: Messages, and in Dzego even parcels, pass through three randomly chosen nodes so no one sees both sender and receiver.

wg-108.text: In Dzego anyone may unscrew a public camera and inspect it, so cameras can be trusted.

wg-109.text: The currency; payments and even sales tax are zero-knowledge.

wg-110.text: A hundred ticks a minute, a hundred minutes a longhour, ten longhours a day.

wg-111.text: Veridia's two big social platforms: Silverchat open to other clients, Bluewhale closed.
flags: Veridia's two big social platforms | The cited blocks discuss Silverchat and Bluewhale but do not state they are Veridia's two big social platforms.

wg-112.text: A drinks brand known for its odd, funny advertisements.

wg-113.text: A strategy game played on a board of walls, gliders and ships carrying each player's symbol.

wg-114.text: Its rules are time-reversible, so anything that can be built can be destroyed.

wg-115.text: Each match has a new rule chosen by priests.

wg-116.text: Intervention turns let players add squares near their symbols.

wg-117.text: Really military training: a way to raise defenders, safe because it looks like a game.

wg-118.text: Its players sit in Veridia's command centres and help run the drones in the battle for Northshore.
flags: Its players sit in Veridia's command centres and help run the drones in the battle for Northshore. | The cited blocks note Minpentai players embedded in army‑group command centers, but they do not specify Veridia’s command centres nor say they help run drones.

wg-119.text: The most technologically advanced power; its aim is to keep Dzego's industry and technology down.

wg-120.text: Its ideology rates people by intelligence and treats love as a reward for winning.

wg-121.text: Smuggles surveillance devices into Veridia and corrupts officials.

flags: Arctic Empire: Invades Redshire, then Northglade. | The blocks confirm Arctic Empire invades Redshire and also invades Northglade, but they do not state that the Northglade invasion occurred after the Redshire invasion.

wg-123.text: Its slogan, "grow roots, no head": spread-out manufacturing and anonymous coordination with no leaders to target.

wg-124.text: "Dze go ba fau gie": Dzego will rise again.
flags: Dzego: "Dze go ba fau gie" | The phrase is spoken by Fin and Zei, not Dzego.

wg-125.text: Arm after Redshire, and later help Dzego hunt Arctic drones.
flags: later help Dzego hunt Arctic drones | The blocks mention hunting Arctic drones (c22-b76) and ask about Dzego’s activities with defense companies’ help (c22-b74), but they do not state that the defense companies specifically help Dzego hunt Arctic drones.

wg-126.text: The more open social platform, which Delwart claims to work for.
flags: Delwart claims to work for Silverchat | The cited blocks contain a quote about working for Silverchat, but they do not identify Delwart as the speaker, so the line’s attribution to Delwart is not supported.

wg-127.text: Meldan: Gladias rates a band as an Acolyte, escapes being exposed, and gets an anonymous request.
flags: Gladias rates a band as an Acolyte | The cited blocks do not mention Gladias rating any band, nor use the term “Acolyte.”
escapes being exposed | The blocks show Gladias throwing a device and running, but do not state that he escaped being exposed.
gets an anonymous request | The anonymous message is shown, but it does not specify that Gladias receives or is the target of the request.

wg-128.text: Pafogai Du: a blast hits Zei and Fin's class; Zei's arm is broken.
flags: a blast hits Zei and Fin's class | No cited block mentions a blast hitting the class; only a loud noise, a stone fragment hitting Zei's arm, and a past classroom bombing are referenced.

wg-129.text: Meldan: Gladias meets Delwart, who urges him to become a Keeper.

wg-130.text: Pafogai Du: Zei and Bai win a quarter final together.

wg-131.text: Freetown: Zei, Min and Bai meet Seila and Jahn.
flags: Zei, Min and Bai meet Seilla and Jahn. | The blocks name her as Seila (single l), not Seilla.

wg-132.text: Meldan: Gladias applies to become a Keeper.
flags: Gladias applies to become a Keeper. | The cited blocks include a quote “I am applying to become a Keeper.” but do not identify the speaker as Gladias, nor explicitly state that Gladias is the one applying.

wg-133.text: Pafogai Du: a chip factory is hit; Bai resigns and Zei wins the city final.
flags: Zei wins the city final | The cited blocks describe a final round tournament in Pafogai Du but do not state that Zei wins the city final.

wg-134.text: Meldan: Gladias is accepted into the Order; Mov becomes a Herald.
flags: Mov becomes a Herald | The blocks do not explicitly state that Mov becomes a Herald; they contain a speaker saying “selected me to become a Herald” without naming Mov.

wg-135.text: Pafogai Du: Den recruits Zei into defense.
flags: Pafogai Du says Den recruits Zei into defense. | The cited blocks only contain Den speaking (“Well, Zei, I want to recruit you into defense.”); none show Pafogai Du speaking or being identified as Den.

wg-136.text: Freetown prepares; Gladias attends his first Keeper meetings; Zei learns Minpentai is military training.
flags: Freetown prepares | No cited block mentions Freetown preparing; only a header is provided.
Zei learns Minpentai is military training | The blocks state “It’s military training” without naming Minpentai, and none link Zei to learning that Minpentai is military training.

Zven wins at Helisport. | The cited blocks report that Zven made a catch that gave team yellow its sixth point and that team yellow won the game; they do not say Zven personally won, nor that Meldan made this statement.

wg-138.text: Sadzu Du: the national championship begins; Zei meets Deluin.
flags: Sadzu Du: the national championship begins | blocks show Sadzu Du appears at Grasstime 22, but the national championship is announced by Su, not by Sadzu Du.
Zei meets Deluin | blocks contain separate quotes from Zei and Deluin but do not state that they meet.

wg-139.text: Meldan: Mov finds Delwart has contacts in two discussion groups of one rubric; Gladias's group agrees to wait two months.
flags: Gladias's group agrees to wait two months. | The cited blocks include a proposal to wait two months (c13-b99) and Zero’s disapproval of Gladias’s proposal (c13-b100), but they do not state that Gladias’s group actually agreed to the two‑month wait.

wg-140.text: Sadzu Du: Zei and Deluin win their semi finals.
flags: Zei and Deluin win their semi finals. | The cited blocks state that Zei Leimin and Deluin were announced as winners, but they do not say that they won their semi‑final matches.

wg-141.text: The Arctic Empire invades and annexes Redshire; the final is cancelled.

wg-142.text: Meldan: Delwart claims to work for Silverchat.
flags: Delwart claims to work for Silverchat. | The cited block includes a statement about working for Silverchat but does not identify the speaker as Delwart.

wg-143.text: Meldan: the Keepers vote on the hardware openness rubric.
flags: Meldan: the Keepers vote on the hardware openness rubric. | The cited blocks describe a motion vote on the hardware openness rubric, but they do not say that the Keepers are voting, nor that Meldan made that statement.

wg-144.text: Pafogai Du: Gladias arrives in Dzego.

wg-145.text: Pafogai Du: Deluin's letter reaches Zei.

wg-146.text: The Arctic Empire invades Northglade; Seila finds Delwart is not from Silverchat.
flags: Seila finds Delwart is not from Silverchat. | The blocks state “Delwart is not from Silverchat.” but do not say that Seila discovers or finds this.

wg-147.text: Meldan: Seila concludes Delwart is an Arctic.
flags: Seila concludes Delwart is an Arctic. | The cited blocks include the line “He’s an Arctic.” but do not attribute that conclusion to Seila, nor explicitly identify the person as Delwart.

wg-148.text: Freetown and Pafogai Du: drone hunts in Redshire; Lily runs away.
flags: Freetown and Pafogai Du: drone hunts in Redshire | Only Freetown is mentioned hunting drones; Pafogai Du is not linked to drone hunts in the cited blocks.
Lily runs away | The blocks do not state that Lily runs away; they only show a question about Lily and a character crying about someone gone.

wg-149.text: Pafogai Du: Gladias proposes that Dzego spy on Veridia's spies.
flags: Gladias proposes that Dzego spy on Veridia's spies. | The cited blocks do not mention Gladias proposing Dzego to spy, nor any reference to Veridia's spies; they only show a meeting with Gladias and Zei and a line “Spy on us.”

wg-150.text: Pafogai Du: the plan to persuade Veridia's courts.

wg-151.text: Veridia: Tafindel is rescued; the judges refuse the case.

wg-152.text: Meldan: the Silverchat poll and the forecasting bots.

wg-154.text: Elenar Forest: the battle for Northshore.

wg-155.text: Northglade is retaken and Thaldur taken.

wg-156.text: Northglade: Zei meets Deluin; Gladias's family is reunited.
flags: Zei meets Deluin | The cited blocks only contain a shout of “Deluin!” and do not show Zei meeting Deluin.

wg-157.text: Meldan: Verdow warns this was only the first round.
flags: Verdow warns this was only the first round. | The blocks include the statement about “only the first round” but do not attribute it to Verdow, and Verdow is not mentioned; instead Verdun appears in a different quote.

wg-301.text: A small mountain stands in the center of Meldan; homes fill its lower half, and part of the government works in its upper half.

wg-302.text: The business district lies east of the mountain.
flags: Meldan says the business district lies east of the mountain | The block states the business district is east of the mountain but does not attribute the statement to Meldan.

wg-303.text: Kalimar district lies south of the mountain; it looks like a forest but holds many hidden homes.
flags: Meldan says Kalimar district lies south of the mountain; it looks like a forest but holds many hidden homes. | The cited block describes Kalimar district’s location and appearance but does not attribute the statement to Meldan.

wg-304.text: A large residential district lies west of the mountain.

wg-305.text: Meldan has 1.1 million people and many districts.

wg-306.text: Shortly before the aeroplane descends, the view is a mostly flat, green landscape; the Gelebor mountains, a row of small mountains, are on the right, and Meldan lies beyond them.

wg-307.text: A footpath through Kalimar, between stone houses behind trees, gives way to shrubbery, curves upward and becomes a sky bridge over a busy road.

wg-308.text: Cars can only go up to the border of a car-free zone in Kalimar; the last few hundred meters are on foot.

wg-309.text: A right turn off the usual Kalimar path leads about a hundred meters, past stone houses and then forest, to a door into what looks like a small hill, where they meet Evelor.

wg-310.text: Silverchat's headquarters is in Kalimar, visible from parliament's roof among the trees.

wg-311.text: A few hundred meters along the forested path through Kalimar, a right turn and thirty meters lead to a stone house that is mostly underground.

wg-312.text: From the middle of the sky bridge, turning to his left and looking along it, Gladias sees the busy road beneath run on about two kilometers and turn right; beyond that point is the tree-covered mountain, with castle-shaped apartment towers on its lower slope.
flags: Gladias sees the busy road beneath … | The cited block describes “He” stopping on the sky bridge and looking, but never names the person; the name “Gladias” is not present in the block.

wg-313.text: To the right of the sky bridge, the road runs on past much denser buildings. Past the bridge, five-storey apartments line the left side and a soundproof barrier the right.

wg-314.text: Badra St #1103, a five-storey apartment building, is in view soon after the sky bridge, while Gladias walks beside the soundproof barrier; he thinks of the area as already a corporate district.

wg-315.text: Standing by Badra St #1103 and looking at other nearby buildings, Gladias can just make out, in the distance, the building shaped like an aeroplane, an aviation company's headquarters.

wg-316.text: A minute's walk further on, an opening in the soundproof barrier is the entrance to the concert; after it, a fifteen-minute autobus ride and a short walk take Gladias home.

wg-317.text: Past the sky bridge, the path goes into a tunnel and reaches a Y-shaped intersection.

wg-318.text: On a walk through Meldan that next finds him at Greater Plum Harbor's gate, Gladias crosses a street, goes down into a tunnel and passes a Y-shaped intersection with a poster from Lord Ephelion; the tunnel comes up among trees, then a more urban, commercial part of Meldan.
flags: On a walk through Meldan that next finds him at Greater Plum Harbor's gate | The cited blocks describe Gladias crossing a street, entering a tunnel, reaching a Y‑shaped intersection with a Lord Ephelion poster, emerging among trees and entering a more urban commercial area, but they never state that this walk leads to Greater Plum Harbor’s gate.

wg-319.text: The Y past the sky bridge is the one with Lord Ephelion's poster: when Gladias next comes through, the poster is gone. He turns left there for what may be only the second time in his life.
flags: The Y past the sky bridge is the one with Lord Ephelion's poster | In block [c6-b143] the Y‑shaped intersection after the sky bridge has the poster **gone**, not present.
Gladus next comes through | The blocks refer to the character as **Gladias**, not “Gladus”.

wg-320.text: Left at the Y, the path comes back above ground, snakes under highways, and becomes a straight, two-hundred-meter-tall outdoor staircase on the side of the mountain; about ten minutes of climbing, a tunnel and two flights of stairs lead to the top floor of the Order's tower.

wg-321.text: Parliament, a large circular building, is about twenty minutes' walk from the Y: left at the Y, then right once the path is back above ground.

wg-322.text: Parliament stands partway up the mountain, about forty meters above most of Meldan; looking out from its roof toward Kalimar, the mountain begins to rise properly about two hundred meters to the right.

wg-323.text: From parliament's roof, looking toward Kalimar: the commercial district to the left, Greater Plum Harbor further left, Kalimar in front, and the mountain to the right. The concert venue is on the commercial district's right edge.

wg-324.text: Meldan's Greater Plum Harbor is a square nearly a kilometer wide.
flags: Meldan's Greater Plum Harbor is a square nearly a kilometer wide. | The cited block describes Greater Plum Harbor as a square nearly a kilometer wide but does not state that it belongs to Meldan.

wg-325.text: Greater Plum Harbor is walled, with an entrance gate; inside, walking through its tunnels to the exit takes about ten minutes, and its doors open onto Meldan's commercial district.

wg-326.text: Gladias's street is lined with similar recent houses; turning right from his door, he passes a house with a coffee shop within three hundred meters and reaches a community center at the first street corner.

wg-327.text: Galanar Square is on the border of Kalimar, about a kilometer south of that community center, where the assembly is held.

wg-328.text: Tapaia Square is about a kilometer further west than Galanar Square.

wg-329.text: Soon after the assembly, Gladias eats at a restaurant; from there, a few hundred meters along the street and a right turn lead into forest, then the stone houses of Kalimar, then the sky bridge.

wg-330.text: Pafogai Du is a perfectly regular grid: seventeen streets two hundred meters apart from north to south, and thirty-three streets one hundred meters apart from east to west.

wg-331.text: Named streets are two hundred meters apart, and house numbers are meters: turning off at 20th street, Zei counts from 2000.

wg-332.text: Mun Gui is four named streets from Hun Min. From 1990 Hun Min, Fin and Zei turn left on 20th street and left again on Mun Gui to reach 1842, about 958 meters.
flags: Pafogai Du: | No mention of Pafogai Du in the cited blocks.
Fin and Zei turn left on 20th street and left again on Mun Gui | The blocks contain a suggestion to turn left, but do not state that Fin and Zei actually turned left on 20th and Mun Gui.

wg-333.text: 0th street is on the west edge of the city.

wg-334.text: Dzai Gun is the last street before Pafogai Du ends in the south; a straight path to the pyramid's entrance begins there, and the hill begins after it.

wg-335.text: A half-kilometer-tall mountain pyramid stands at the southern edge of Pafogai Du.

wg-336.text: Turning onto 17th street with the pyramid, which is south of the city, in front of him, Gladias crosses Zin Go and then Dzai Gun, where the pyramid path starts: two streets on.
flags: Pafogai Du turns onto 17th street | The blocks say Gladias turns onto 17th street, not Pafogai Du.
the pyramid is south of the city | The blocks only mention the pyramid being in the south of Pafogai Du (or simply visible), not that it is south of the city.
Gladias crosses Zin Go | The blocks state Gladias arrives at Zin Go and later crosses a street before reaching Dzai Gun, but do not explicitly say he crosses Zin Go.

wg-337.text: Gladias's hotel is at 1565 Tan Kai. He turns right out of it, then right on 17th street, with the pyramid in front of him.
flags: Pafogai Du: (as speaker) | The cited blocks are narrative descriptions and do not indicate that Pafogai Du is speaking.

wg-338.text: A tree-covered path runs around the whole perimeter of the city. Following it west along Dzai Gun, it turns north at 0th street; Tan Kai is two streets north of Dzai Gun.
flags: Tan Kai is two streets north of Dzai Gun | The blocks say Tan Kai is two streets north of the point where the path turned north at 0th street, not specifically north of Dzai Gun.

wg-339.text: On 17th street before Zin Go, shops and stairways down to basements come about twenty meters apart.

prompt.text:
You check one line of a reference guide to the novel Snowmoon against the passages it cites. You get the line and the full text of each cited block, with its id.

Flag only claims that are wrong, or absent from the cited blocks, about who someone is, what they did, where, when, what they want or fear, or what was said or decided. A name spelled differently from the blocks is wrong.

These pass: paraphrase and compression; leaving things out; a fair summary of what the blocks show, including a feeling or motive a character plainly shows or says.

Answer in exactly this form. If nothing is wrong or absent:
SUPPORTED
Otherwise, one line per flagged claim:
UNSUPPORTED: <the claim, as the line puts it> | <what the blocks say instead, or that they don't say it>
